Thus the parabola is y=-x^2-2x+3 and its axis of symmetry is x=-1, so write P=(-1,t). Then test the three possible right-angle vertices in triangle BPC using dot products: right angle at P gives (B-P)·(C-P)=0; right angle at B gives (P-B)·(C-B)=0; right angle at C gives (P-C)·(B-C)=0. Solving these equations gives t=(3±sqrt(17))/2, t=-2, and t=4, hence the four coordinates of P.

2. The right angle is at B: vector P-B=(2,t), C-B=(3,3). The dot product is 0: 2·3+t·3=0, obtaining 6+3t=0, so t=-2.

3. The right angle is at C: vector P-C=(-1,t-3), B-C=(-3,-3). The dot product is 0: (-1)(-3)+(t-3)(-3)=0, obtaining 12-3t=0, so t=4.

Therefore there are four points P satisfying the conditions in total.
